result.summary: I reviewed only the four supplied VS Code test and fixture files. I found no concrete, reachable defect in them. The assigned obligations are mostly about the JetBrains/Kotlin side and about production sources that were not supplied. Those sources include the Kotlin files, gateway.ts, session-owner.ts, and the shared controllers under src/shared/connection-manager. For that reason, no obligation can be shown to hold or not hold from this batch. This is a manual workaround review, not a canonical CR, and it does not approve BUILD.

obligations.evidence: The tests exercise the mutation, unknown-state reconcile, and busy refusal paths. For example, a second submit of the same target rejects with `busy`, and a refresh failure keeps `refresh:'failed'` with no empty-list fallback. They also cover replay gating and root switch A→B→A. The ConnectionManagerState projection itself (listState values, filter, draftRevision, dirty) and the manager model source were not supplied, so I could not check them.

The TS-side behaviour is consistent with the SafeConnection invariants. Tests assert that credentials are not echoed (`fixture-only-private` and `signature` absent from records). They also assert that cleanup requests send `{ticket}` only, and that the remove request keys are exactly expectedRevision/key/mode/operationId/ticket. The Kotlin DTOs/decoders and DaemonGatewayService/UnixSocketDaemonRpc were not supplied.

No JetBrains files (ConnectionsSessionService, Gateway, Panel, Configurable, plugin.xml, action) were supplied. The VS Code fixture `forkOwner` creates separate owners with separate lanes, but that does not cover the JetBrains project isolation. Live JetBrains UI is deferred-user.
There is no Kotlin evidence. DaemonGatewayService and its tests were not supplied.
The Kotlin ConnectionProtocol.kt and its CM-S5-WIRE-KT test were not supplied. The TS tests load the shared corpus through `loadConnectionCorpus()`, but Kotlin parity cannot be judged from them.
The Kotlin PROJECT Disposable session service and the CM-S5-OWNER-KT test were not supplied. Only the VS Code ConnectionsWorkbenchOwner is exercised, indirectly.

The Kotlin Delete/Discard presentation and tests were not supplied. The TS counterpart test removal.test.ts is consistent with the requirements. It covers zero-effect Cancel, busy/conflict/unknown states, and ticket-only independent cleanup. Cleanup stays tied to the original ticket after same-ID recreation, and source file bytes are unchanged. It also covers 20 sc6 snapshots, and Discard for temporary rows. This is TS evidence only.

The fixture has capability modes (missing/old/future/malformed, omitted features). It also has legacy `db.saveConnection`/`db.deleteConnection` traps with a `legacyWrites()` counter, plus `legacyList`. The compat test that asserts on them was not in the supplied batch. Kotlin-side compat was not supplied either.

limitations: Only test and fixture files were supplied. The production sources they exercise (connections/gateway.ts, session-owner.ts, src/shared/connection-manager/*, the daemon RPC) were not included.
No JetBrains/Kotlin evidence was supplied, so three of the assigned obligations (data-model:9, invariant:3, and the Kotlin plan tasks) cannot be assessed here.
I did not run the tests, per the no-tool-calls instruction. The recorded VS Code 0.5.23 manual testing is user-reported, and the JetBrains live UI is deferred. I did not treat either as a pass.
No supplied changed file was left unassessed, but each was only read statically.
